fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E P/E (haircut EPS $4.50 x 9x = $40.5), 2028E EV/EBITDA at a below-spot $5.50/lb copper deck (~$690M x 6x less ~$150M net debt = $37.3) and 0.85x an estimated ~$45 NAV ($38.3); weighted 35/40/25 gives ~$38.6, essentially the current price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027E EPS $4.50 (consensus $4.79 from 13 analysts, haircut ~6% for Ero's history of guidance misses and Pilar ramp risk) x 9x (discount to diversified copper peers for single-country Brazil risk, BRL exposure and copper near record highs ~$6.70/lb)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E: 85kt Cu (~187 Mlb, mid of 80-90kt outlook) x 96% payable x ($5.50 deck - $2.20 C1) = ~$592M + Xavantina 60koz x ($3,800 - $1,200) = ~$156M - ~$60M G&A/exploration = ~$690M EBITDA; 6.0x = $4.14B EV; less ~$150M projected net debt at end-2027 (from $453M at Q2-26, falling on FCF with capex past peak); / ~107M diluted shares

methods.name: other (P/NAV)
methods.inputs: Estimated NAV ~$45/sh at long-term copper ~$4.75-5.00/lb (sell-side NAVs imply BofA 0.8x P/NAV around C$45-49 targets) plus modest Furnas option value (60% earn-in, PFS 2027, FID 2029); 0.85x P/NAV for a producing mid-tier with Brazil risk

bear.story: Copper mean-reverts from record ~$6.70/lb toward $4.50-5.00 as China demand weakens and backwardation unwinds; Pilar shaft ramp slips into 2028+, Caraiba/Tucuma costs overrun on strong BRL and inflation, 2027 guidance disappoints again (as at the Sept CMD); stock re-rates to ~4.5x depressed EBITDA.

base.story: Copper stays elevated but off the peak ($5.50-6.00/lb); 2026 lands in 67.5-77.5kt guidance, 2027 production ~75-80kt with capex falling sharply after the 2026 peak; revolver repaid and a modest shareholder-return program announced; stock trades ~8-9x earnings near fair value.

bull.story: Copper holds or exceeds $6.50-7.00/lb in a structural deficit; Pilar shaft completes on schedule (bottom by YE26) and Tucuma filtration expansion lifts throughput; FCF $400M+ drives net cash by late 2027, buybacks/dividend, and a positive Furnas PFS; re-rating toward peer multiples (~6.5-7x EV/EBITDA on $900M+ EBITDA).

thesis_break_reason: Around $23 (~-40%) the stock would be pricing either copper falling back below ~$4.50/lb or a material operational failure (Pilar shaft delay, Tucuma underperformance, cost blowout) that pushes 2028 production well below the 80-90kt outlook; at that level EV would be only ~3.5-4x my base 2028 EBITDA, which ordinary volatility alone should not produce once leverage is below 1x.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 production results (H2-weighted copper and gold ramp)
Q3 2026 financial results; FX hedge gains, revolver repayment, possible shareholder-return framework
Pilar shaft sinking targeted to reach shaft bottom by year-end; Tucuma modular filters commissioning in Q4
FY2026 results, 2027 guidance and updated three-year outlook; Tucuma reserve update
Q1 2027 results; historic gold concentrate sales winding down by mid-2027
Furnas pre-feasibility study (Vale Base Metals earn-in)
Copper price (record ~$6.83/lb Comex on 2026-09-22), USD/BRL, China demand data

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: stock is highly levered; each $0.50/lb move changes EBITDA by ~$85-90M (~$0.80/sh EPS)
Pilar shaft execution and timing of the 2028 production step-up to 80-90kt
Brazil cost inflation and BRL strength (hedge book at 5.54 floor rolls off; C1 guidance $2.15-2.35/lb with ~$0.10/lb upside risk)
Ero's track record of guidance revisions; weaker multi-year outlook flagged at Sept 14 Capital Markets Day and subsequent downgrades
Timing and size of shareholder returns vs. Furnas funding needs
reasoning: Ero Copper (NYSE/TSX: ERO) is a Brazil-focused copper-gold producer (Caraiba, Tucuma, Xavantina). The stock doubled over the past year mainly because copper hit records (Comex ~$6.70/lb on 9/25, up ~42% y/y) and the balance sheet de-risked: Q2-26 adj. EBITDA $144M, adj. EPS $0.83, CFO $138M, net debt down to $453M (0.8x), with a further $25M revolver repayment, and 2026 as peak capex. Against that, the Sept 14 Capital Markets Day reiterated a 2026-28 outlook (Caraiba 35-50kt, Tucuma 32.5-40kt, 80-90kt by 2028) but was read as weaker volumes and higher costs, triggering downgrades (BofA, BTG, Bradesco BBI, Freedom Broker); consensus target ~C$48 (~US$35) sits below the price, CIBC C$56 (~US$40) Neutral, BMO C$52 Outperform. Consensus 2027 EPS $4.79 puts the stock at ~7.9x P/E and ~5-5.5x EV/EBITDA on spot copper, which looks cheap, but those estimates capitalise near-record copper. My three valuation methods (P/E, EV/EBITDA at a $5.50 deck, P/NAV) cluster at $37-41, blending to ~$38.6, essentially today's $37.87, so I expect no drift from valuation. Scenario mean (~$38.8) is also near spot. For the distribution I used a lognormal with median ~$35.5 and sigma ~0.50 (below the 64% realized vol, which was inflated by a one-way copper rally, but well above the 25-35% large-cap base rate given a mid-cap single-country miner levered to copper), slightly fattening the left tail for a copper-price reversal from record highs. That puts P(>= $38) at ~0.45 and P(>= $23) at ~0.80. Research relied on the Q2 2026 6-K, Q2 call transcript summary, CMD summaries, analyst-action news and Alpha Vantage consensus; no option data used; the full CMD deck with 2027 cost guidance was not found, so that detail is inferred from press coverage.
